75848-hearts-and-clubs.title: Hearts And Clubs
75848-hearts-and-clubs.creator: Unknown
75848-hearts-and-clubs.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. I cannot very well spend my evening spelling out the advertisements on one side of the paper. (_Sarcastically_) Perhaps I may be able to find a newspaper of a single sheet only--one of those patent-inside arrangements--if so, I certainly shall take it. (_Getting up_) Since I am so unpleasantly distracting, I had better leave you in peace. They don’t mind speaking above a whisper at the club. (_Throws down paper and takes up his hat_) Good-night; don’t sit up for me.

arxiv-2102-00797.title: Uncertainty evaluation and correlation analysis of single-particle energies in phenomenological nuclear mean field: An investigation of propagating uncertainties for independent model parameters
arxiv-2102-00797.creator: Zhen-Zhen Zhang, Hua-Lei Wang, Hai-Yan Meng, Min-Liang Liu
arxiv-2102-00797.description: Abstract Based on Monte Carlo approach and conventional error analysis theory, taking the heaviest doubly magic nucleus 208 Pb as an example, we firstly evaluate the propagated uncertainties of universal potential parameters for three typical types of single-particle energies in the phenomenological Woods-Saxon mean field.

arxiv-2102-01325.title: FLOSS != GitHub: A Case Study of Linux/BSD Perceptions from Microsoft’s Acquisition of GitHub
arxiv-2102-01325.creator: Raula Gaikovina Kula 1 , Hideki Hata 1 , Kenichi Matsumoto 1
arxiv-2102-01325.description: Abstract In 2018, the software industry giants Microsoft made a move into the Open Source world by completing the acquisition of mega Open Source platform, GitHub. This acquisition was not without controversy, as it is well-known that the free software communities includes not only the ability to use software freely, but also the libre nature in Open Source Software.

arxiv-2103-01225.title: The superconducting circuit companion – an introduction with worked examples
arxiv-2103-01225.creator: S. E. Rasmussen, K. S. Christensen, S. P. Pedersen, L. B. Kristensen, T. Bækkegaard, N. J. S. Loft, N. T. Zinner
arxiv-2103-01225.description: Abstract This tutorial aims at giving an introductory treatment of the circuit analysis of superconducting qubits, i.e., two-level systems in superconducting circuits. It also touches upon couplings between such qubits and how microwave driving and these couplings can be used for single- and two-qubit gates, as well as how to include noise when calculating the dynamics of the system.

arxiv-2103-06497.title: ON SYNTHETIC ABSORPTION LINE PROFILES OF THERMALLY DRIVEN WINDS FROM ACTIVE GALACTIC NUCLEI
arxiv-2103-06497.creator: Shalini Ganguly, Daniel Proga, Tim Waters, Randall C. Dannen, Sergei Dyda, Margherita Giustini, Timothy Kallman, John Raymond, Jon Miller, Paola Rodriguez Hidalgo
arxiv-2103-06497.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shalini Ganguly, Daniel Proga, Tim Waters, Randall C. Dannen, Sergei Dyda, Margherita Giustini, Timothy Kallman, John Raymond, Jon Miller, Paola Rodriguez Hidalgo. The warm absorbers observed in more than half of all nearby active galactic nuclei (AGN) are tracers of ionized outflows located at parsec scale distances from the central engine.

arxiv-2110-09618.title: Interpolating Between Sampling and Variational Inference with Infinite Stochastic Mixtures
arxiv-2110-09618.creator: Richard D. Lange, Ari S. Benjamin, Ralf M. Haefner ∗, Xaq Pitkow ∗
arxiv-2110-09618.description: Abstract Sampling and Variational Inference (VI) are two large families of methods for approximate inference that have complementary strengths. Sampling methods excel at approximating arbitrary probability distributions, but can be inefficient. VI methods are efficient, but may misrepresent the true distribution. Here, we develop a general framework where approximations are stochastic mixtures of simple component distributions.

arxiv-2202-06381.title: Pleasant behavior of swampland conjectures in the face of specific inflationary models
arxiv-2202-06381.description: Abstract Recently researchers have been studying various conditions as swampland criteria in cosmological implications. They have studied many inflation models with different swampland conditions. Occasionally these conjectures are modified and lead to fascinating points. The swampland conjecture is in contradiction with the slow-roll single-field inflation model.

arxiv-2206-10153.title: Experimental implementation of finite-time Carnot cycle
arxiv-2206-10153.creator: Ruo-Xun Zhai, Fang-Ming Cui, Yu-Han Ma, C. P. Sun, Hui Dong
arxiv-2206-10153.description: Abstract The Carnot cycle is a prototype of ideal heat engine to draw mechanical energy from the heat flux between two thermal baths with the maximum efficiency, dubbed as the Carnot efficiency η C \eta_{\mathrm{C}} . Such efficiency can only be reached by thermodynamical equilibrium processes with infinite time, accompanied unavoidably with vanishing power - energy output per unit time.

arxiv-2302-07398.title: Direct evidence of terahertz emission arising from anomalous Hall effect
arxiv-2302-07398.creator: Venkatesh Mottamchetty, Parul Rani, Rimantas Brucas, Anders Rydberg, Peter Svedlindh, Rahul Gupta
arxiv-2302-07398.description: Abstract A detailed understanding of the different mechanisms being responsible for terahertz (THz) emission in ferromagnetic (FM) materials will aid in designing efficient THz emitters. In this report, we present direct evidence of THz emission from single layer Co 0.4 Fe 0.4 B 0.2 (CoFeB) FM thin films.

arxiv-2304-14929.title: Geometry and distribution of roots of μ 2 ≡ D mod m \mu^{2}\equiv D\bmod m with D ≡ 1 mod 4 D\equiv 1\bmod 4
arxiv-2304-14929.creator: Zonglin Li, Matthew Welsh
arxiv-2304-14929.description: Abstract We extend the geometric interpretation of the roots of the quadratic congruence μ 2 ≡ D ( mod m ) \mu^{2}\equiv D\pmod{m} as the tops of certain geodesics in the hyperbolic plane to the case when D D is square-free and D ≡ 1 ( mod 4 ) D\equiv 1\pmod{4} .

arxiv-2402-10797.title: BlackJAX: Composable Bayesian inference in JAX Thanks: Department of Mathematics and Statistics, Lancaster University, UK Thanks: Department of Electrical Engineering and Automation, Aalto University, Finland Thanks: Google, Switzerland Thanks: .txt, France
arxiv-2402-10797.description: Abstract BlackJAX is a library implementing sampling and variational inference algorithms commonly used in Bayesian computation. It is designed for ease of use, speed, and modularity by taking a functional approach to the algorithm’s implementation. Designed from basic components to specific iterative procedures, BlackJAX allows the end user to build and experiment with new algorithms by composition.

arxiv-2411-01768.title: Isomorphic gcd-graphs over polynomial rings Thanks: JM is partially supported by the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) grant R0370A01. He gratefully acknowledges the Western University Faculty of Science Distinguished Professorship 2020-2021. He is also grateful for
arxiv-2411-01768.creator: Ján Mináč, Tung T. Nguyen, Nguy ê ~ \tilde{\text{\^{e}}} n Duy Tân
arxiv-2411-01768.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ján Mináč, Tung T. Nguyen, Nguy ê ~ \tilde{\text{\^{e}}} n Duy Tân. Gcd-graphs over the ring of integers modulo n n are a simple and elegant class of integral graphs. The study of these graphs connects multiple areas of mathematics, including graph theory, number theory, and ring theory. In a recent work, inspired by the analogy between number fields and function fields, we define and study gcd-graphs over polynomial rings with coefficients in finite fields.

arxiv-2507-09399.description: Abstract . Multi-norm singular integrals and Fourier multipliers were introduced in [ 29 ] , and one application of these notions was a precise description of the composition of convolution operators with Calderón-Zygmund kernels adapted to n n different families of dilations.

arxiv-2509-12425.title: Une caractérisation de 𝔹 dR + {\mathbb{B}}_{\rm dR}^{\scriptscriptstyle+} et 𝒪 ​ 𝔹 dR + {\mathcal{O}}{\mathbb{B}}_{\rm dR}^{\scriptscriptstyle+}
arxiv-2509-12425.creator: Pierre Colmez
arxiv-2509-12425.description: Abstract Résumé Nous montrons que 𝐁 dR + {\bf B}_{\rm dR}^{+} est l’épaississement universel de 𝐂 p {\bf C}_{p} . Plus généralement, nous montrons que, si S S est une algèbre affinoïde réduite, 𝒪 ​ 𝔹 dR + ​ ( S ¯ ) {\mathcal{O}}{\mathbb{B}}_{\rm dR}^{\scriptscriptstyle+}({\overline{S}}) est le S S -épaississement universel du complété de S ¯ {\overline{S}} .

arxiv-2510-06624.title: KANAZAWA-25-04 Phase structure analysis of 2d lattice CP(1) model with θ \theta term using tensor renormalization group method
arxiv-2510-06624.creator: Hayato Aizawa, Shinji Takeda, Yusuke Yoshimura
arxiv-2510-06624.description: Abstract We investigate the phase structure of a two-dimensional lattice CP(1) model with a θ \theta term. In particular, we aim to identify a critical region expected to exist along a θ = π \theta=\pi line. To explore the phase structure non-perturbatively and avoid the sign problem, we employ the tensor renormalization group method.

arxiv-2601-04797.title: The Semigeostrophic-Euler Limit: Lifespan Lower Bounds and O ⁡ ( ε ) O(\varepsilon) Velocity Stability
arxiv-2601-04797.creator: Victor Armegioiu
arxiv-2601-04797.description: Abstract . We study the two-dimensional semigeostrophic (SG ε ) system on the torus in the small-amplitude scaling and its convergence to incompressible Euler in the dual (geostrophic) formulation. Within a natural bootstrap regime for the Poisson/Monge–Ampère coupling, we obtain two main results.

arxiv-2602-14625.title: Near-Linear Time Computation of Welzl Orders on Graphs with Linear Neighborhood Complexity
arxiv-2602-14625.creator: Jan Dreier, Clemens Kuske
arxiv-2602-14625.description: Abstract Orders with low crossing number, introduced by Welzl, are a fundamental tool in range searching and computational geometry. Recently, they have found important applications in structural graph theory: set systems with linear shatter functions correspond to graph classes with linear neighborhood complexity.

plos-pone-0001227.creator: Mathieu Lévesque, Samuel Gatien, Kenneth Finnson et al.
plos-pone-0001227.description: PLOS ONE research article. Axolotls (urodele amphibians) have the unique ability, among vertebrates, to perfectly regenerate many parts of their body including limbs, tail, jaw and spinal cord following injury or amputation. The axolotl limb is the most widely used structure as an experimental model to stu

pmc-10531890.title: Diabetic Endothelial Cell Glycogen Synthase Kinase 3β Activation Induces VCAM1 Ectodomain Shedding
pmc-10531890.creator: Masuma Akter Brishti, Somasundaram Raghavan, Kennedy Lamar, Udai P Singh, Daniel M Collier, M Dennis Leo, Catherine Davis
pmc-10531890.description: Soluble cell adhesion molecules (sCAMs) are secreted ectodomain fragments of surface adhesion molecules, ICAM1 and VCAM1. sCAMs have diverse immune functions beyond their primary function, impacting immune cell recruitment and activation. Elevated sVCAM1 levels have been found to be associated with poor cardiovascular disease (CVD) outcomes, supporting VCAM1’s role as a potential diagnostic marker and therapeutic target.

pmc-10586261.title: Effects of Synthetic Tetronamides and Methylated Denigrins on Bacterial Quorum Sensing and Biofilm Formation
pmc-10586261.creator: Sweta Roy, Jaime A. M. Acosta, Milandip Karak, Isabela Ramirez-Velez, Kohei Torikai, Dacheng Ren, Luiz C. A. Barbosa
pmc-10586261.description: Detrimental biofilms of bacterial pathogens cause chronic infections with a high-level tolerance to antibiotics. To identify new control agents, we synthesized and tested a total of 14 tetronamides (including 5 new compounds) and 6 denigrin intermediates on the model species Escherichia coli.

pmc-11862320.title: Addiction Transfer Post Bariatric Surgery- A Case Report
pmc-11862320.creator: S. Haugh, H. Belay, P. Cromwell
pmc-11862320.description: Introduction Bariatric surgery is an effective treatment for patients with obesity. Rates of obesity are increasing worldwide as are the number of bariatric procedures performed. Following bariatric surgery patients have increased contact with psychiatric services, there is an increased risk of deliberate self-harm, suicide attempts and completed suicide.

pmc-12459619.title: Tocilizumab for Non-Infectious Uveitis: A Systematic Review
pmc-12459619.creator: Haixing Cao, Kaiyu Bian, Cong Ma, Naiwen Zhang, Xiang Ma
pmc-12459619.description: Non-infectious uveitis (NIU) comprises a heterogeneous group of diseases causing severe ocular inflammation that threatens vision. In addition to visual impairment, patients frequently endure chronic pain, functional disorders, and psychosocial stress, all of which substantially reduce quality of life. Treating NIU remains challenging because many patients respond inadequately to high-dose corticosteroids and various immunosuppressants.

pmc-12520722.title: Patrones electroencefalográficos y su asociación con el pronóstico funcional en encefalitis autoinmune anti-NMDA
pmc-12520722.creator: Christian Alejandro Aguilar-Vázquez, Nallely Denisse Ruvalcaba-Sánchez, Julián Alberto Hernández-Domínguez, Sergio De Jesús Aguilar Castillo
pmc-12520722.description: Resumen Introducción:la encefalitis autoinmune es una enfermedad de poca incidencia y prevalencia, pero que presenta altas tasas de incapacidad y puede ser potencialmente mortal. Objetivo:determinar si la presencia de patrones anormales electroencefalográficos en pacientes con encefalitis autoinmune anti-NMDAR afectan con el pronóstico funcional a los 3 meses. Material y métodos:se realizó un estudio retrospectivo, observacional, analítico, longitudinal-transversal, con cohorte retrospectiva.

pmc-12521350.title: The chemobrain in breast cancer patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12521350.creator: Lidvine Godaert, Moustapha Dramé
pmc-12521350.description: The aim of the study was to determine the incidence of chemobrain in breast cancer patients, define it, and review the various tools used to measure it. A comprehensive literature review was performed, and covered all publications up to and including September 30, 2024.

pmc-12847700.title: Effectiveness of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir and molnupiravir in reducing the risk of short-term and long-term cardiovascular complications of COVID-19: a target trial emulation study
pmc-12847700.creator: Zihao Guo, Yuchen Wei, Guozhang Lin, Katherine Min Jia, Christopher Boyer, Huwen Wang, Conglu Li, Chi Tim Hung, Carrie Ho Kwan Yam, Tsz Yu Chow, Shi Zhao, Kehang Li, Aimin Yang, Chris Ka Pun Mok, David SC Hui, Eng Kiong Yeoh, Ka Chun Chong
pmc-12847700.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). While treatment with nirmatrelvir/ritonavir or molnupiravir is effective in lowering the rate of severe COVID-19, the effectiveness of these antivirals in reducing the risk of cardiovascular outcomes, especially among the hospitalized population, remains largely unknown. In this study, we assessed the real-world effectiveness of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir and molnupiravir on short- and long-term cardiovascular complications of COVID-19 using a target trial emulation design. Two target trials of COVID-19 antivirals were emulated by using a territory-wide, population-based, retrospective cohort of hospitalized patients in Hong Kong.

pmc-13076947.title: TensoGraph: a tensor–transformer framework for global–local drug synergy prediction on heterogeneous graphs
pmc-13076947.creator: Xi Wang, Dongxue Zhang, Limin Li
pmc-13076947.description: Combination therapy, which administers multiple drugs either simultaneously or sequentially, aims to enhance therapeutic efficacy while minimizing side effects and drug resistance common in monotherapies for complex diseases. Identifying drug combinations that exhibit synergistic effects is therefore critical to both biomedical research and clinical practice.

pmc-13226070.title: A glycan-based adjuvant expands the breadth and duration of protection of mRNA-based vaccines
pmc-13226070.creator: Kautilya K. Jena, Pengxiang Qu, Lauren Baracco, Shahab Saghaei, Keerti, Zahra Allahyari, Daniel Boehmer, Moriah Mitchell, Carly A. Dillen, Hai-Yun Li, Enqi Liu, Valentina Poli, Océane Dufies, David P. Hoytema van Konijnenburg, Roberto Spreafico, Caihong Bi, Rebecca Hall, Michael D. Kruppa, Zuchao Ma
pmc-13226070.description: The activation of pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) orchestrates inflammation and regulates adaptive immunity. To test whether tuning inflammation through PRR stimulation enhanced the efficacy of mRNA vaccines, we combined an mRNA-based vaccine generated against the ancestral spike protein of SARS-CoV-2 with mannadjuvant, a formulation of fungal mannan and aluminum hydroxide targeting the PRR dectin-2.

pmc-13356944.title: Free Riding on the Harm Principle
pmc-13356944.creator: Lucie White
pmc-13356944.description: There are two main ways in which a mandatory vaccination policy is often defended—by accusing vaccine refusers of ‘free riding’, or by appealing to the ‘harm principle’. In their recent book, Roland Pierik and Marcel Verweij take the latter approach—an attractive option, as they note, due to the wide acceptance of the harm principle.
